reviews.title: PLEASE THINK TWICE BEFORE SUBSCRIBING.
reviews.text:
I genuinely wanted to enjoy this app. I downloaded Haven with the intention of having a place to grow in my relationship with God, learn more about the Bible, and strengthen my faith. Unfortunately, my experience has been incredibly disappointing, and I would strongly encourage anyone considering downloading this app to think twice before giving them their money.

First, the subscription situation is frustrating and incredibly unclear. The app presents itself as though there may be an option to use it for free, even offering a “Try it free before deleting” option when attempting to leave. However, when I actually tried to access that offer, absolutely nothing happened. If there is a free version, why make it so difficult to access? And if there isn’t one, why create the impression that users have another option?

Second, and perhaps most frustratingly, I attempted to cancel my subscription, only to find myself charged not once, but twice. That’s approximately $14 for a subscription advertised at around $7 per week. These charges happened within the same week, yet the app subsequently acted as though I hadn’t even paid for access. Imagine having your money taken twice and then being told you don’t have an active subscription. There is something seriously wrong with that experience.

I understand that app developers need to make money. I understand that subscriptions exist and that creating and maintaining an app requires resources. My issue isn’t simply that this app costs mon

reviews.title: The score card
reviews.text:
As an inspirational app, requiring users to visit every day or risk losing their “streak” adds unnecessary pressure.

We already face so much pressure to perform, engage, and maintain streaks across today’s social media platforms. Bringing that same dynamic into a space intended to inspire and uplift feels counterproductive and, ultimately, discouraging.

reviews.title: The Lords Love should be Free. The creator is not a believer in Faith, only wants money.
reviews.text:
I went through the whole process of answering the questions and wanting to build my relationship with Jesus, our almighty lord. I immediately got turned off and uninstalled when it said I was connected to a “free trial” that would turn into a monthly/annual payment. I don’t have a deep connection with faith and the lord but I know he would be disappointed in the creators of this app, using faith as a money grab is a low blow. The people seeking this help often can’t afford this payment program. Also the Lords love and message is free, charging for it is sinful. This app is not what it portrays itself to be. As someone opening up to faith I know the creators of this app are not believers themselves. If they were they would not CHARGE MONEY for gods words. Very disappointing and outright shameful.

After extensive research, the creator has done all he can to wipe his net worth and religious practice from the internet. If you’re someone who created this app with the right intentions, to be closer with our almighty lord, then you have no reason to hide that info. If you know what group typically lies and manipulates the masses then you know this app is nothing but a money grab for someone in that practice. Don’t let them make a mockery of our lord and don’t pay for anything, uninstall this app and go buy a bible. Don’t pay the evil to manipulate and take advantage of gods words.

reviews.title: The Worst app purchase to date
reviews.text: I was so excited about it this app but after not being reminded to cancel as they would, it was too late to get my money back. They send me dead links after complaining. The quizzes and memory verses are repetitive after using only after a week! It’s a very expensive app that doesn’t even try. I think it’s a bait app that just wants your money. Please make more things since now I have to have the app for a whole year.

reviews.title: Annual subscription charged without the promised notice
reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience. The app stated that I would be notified before the subscription was charged, but I never received that notice.

Instead, I was charged for a full annual subscription without any prior warning. I relied on the app’s own statement that I would be notified before the subscription started or the charge was made. Had I received the promised notice, I would have cancelled and would not have agreed to the annual subscription.

What makes this even more disappointing is that this is a Christian app. A service built around faith and Christian values should be especially transparent and trustworthy with its users. Charging someone without the notice that was explicitly promised feels completely inconsistent with those values.

I have requested an immediate cancellation and a full refund. I strongly recommend that users be very careful with the subscription terms in this app.

reviews.title: Paywalling God is wild business behavior
reviews.text: I was so excited for this because the concept is honestly beautiful, but of course, it’s ruined by greed. Literally every single actual widget feature is locked behind a paid subscription. If you don’t pay, you just get a basic daily notification. Why advertise beautiful home screen widgets if you’re going to paywall the entire app? Capitalizing on Scripture like this is actually wild. God is free. Faith is free. Charging people a monthly premium just to have His word on their home screen is so nasty and scummy. Do better.

reviews.title: Beware, DEI app, Not a Christian app
reviews.text: Yes I was getting daily bible verses as pop ups. Then when I responded to whether I needed prayer for anything I got an answer I was not expecting. To sum it up, in response to my request they referenced a “higher power” instead of God? When I asked why they stated “Using “higher power” allows for inclusivity, honoring the diverse ways people understand the divine. For some, this is God, while others might see it differently. It’s a way to respect each individuals unique spiritual journey without assuming specific beliefs”. SORRY, this app is not based on true Christian values or Bible theology. There is only one GOD, Jesus Christ!

reviews.title: Unwanted subscription pending
reviews.text: It seems as though all of the negative reviews are the same. I’m experiencing the same thing. I was told that I will get a heads up to cancel. That didn’t happen, but I did remember on the third day to cancel the free trial.. But before I can cancel on the third day, they tried to take a payment, but my card was locked so a payment couldn’t be taken. Now I have a pending charge of $63 after taxes. I called Apple customer service to report the problem. They said there’s nothing that they could do because it’s a pending charge. There is no phone number to contact customer service for a resolution. You can’t even leave an email or do a chat even though a “chat” is available. Please remove this pending charge.

reviews.title: Limited Bible verses, found a FREE app instead
reviews.text:
My only issue with it is that it seems to give the same several Bible verses over and over. I’ve had it for about a month now and I see the same rotation of verses on my Lock Screen all the time. I don’t have any filters set up to limit it in this way. I have paid for the entire year so I will use it until the subscription is up but probably won’t resubscribe because of this.

Update: they reached out to me to try and rectify the issue. I submit more details via their requested method and it has been about a few months. I have still not seen any improvement. I switched to the Bible Chat app, it has the same exact feature and it is FREE. Would have never downloaded this one in the first place if I knew about that one.

reviews.title: Money grab
reviews.text: This is just a data collecting survey with a money grab at the end. You cannot use the app until providing survey level data, and then you only get 3 days before needing to pay. Apps should be allowed to make money, but potential users should know this app doesn’t just have in-app purchases—it’s most basic use requires a paid subscription. And if you’re just looking for lock screen widgets, carefully consider what you’re willing to trade for that (personal data, money).

It was not what I anticipated, but worse, no way to work with them. Would not recommend. Other options with actual support exist, I am sure.

reviews.title: Overpriced
reviews.text: My dissatisfaction comes from two main issues. The first, as I was using the app I didn’t like how some of the Bible quotes were not biblical at all, they were just quotes. It became clear quickly how useless for me, the app was. The second part to the problem is - as life tends to get busy around the holiday times and I’m trying to support a family member who’s fallen on hard times; I - your everyday human being -forgot to cancel the trial subscription. Now I’m in an endless queue of being charged for something I do not want. This is preventing me from doing a lot of things with my apple account as you can imagine. All in all, $35 is ridiculous for what this app offers you. The Haven app, is definitely  my go to which is well worth that price point. Please use better discernment than I have.

reviews.text: I have had a streak for over 100+ days and really enjoyed the app but unfortunately I feel that there is a political agenda being pushed down my throat. Not once but TWICE have I gotten quotes from Charlie K*rk, and while I understand there are some viewpoints in Christianity that are deemed conservative, aligning your religious app with someone who was known for spreading hate and discrimination is really disheartening. I unfortunately will not continue to use this app because I don’t think that these quotes were added by accident and while I cannot change the beliefs of the app creators I definitely don’t think this is an app for me.
